_note: Which provider reaches which of the platform's models. Generated by
scripts/build_model_providers.py and committed, so an installation
offers the list without asking any provider anything.
Keys under 'reach' are the BARE model names of model_register.json.
The value is the id THAT provider wants, verbatim -- the prefix in
front of it is what makes it a platform model id.
'declared' is kept by hand and no run of the script touches it: a
provider whose id the register's name cannot match stands there with
the source that says the two are the same model.
A provider under 'providers' with answered: false did not answer on
the day this file was generated. Its reason is recorded, so a short
list says why it is short -- and its entries under 'reach' are what
the last run that reached it wrote, from the day 'kept_from' names.

glm-5.3._note: Mistral serves Z.ai's GLM 5.3 under the id zai-glm-5-3, with the aliases zai-glm-5 and zai-glm-latest; its catalogue entry for that id reads "Official Z.ai GLM 5.3 model". No bare glm-5-3 exists there, so the register's name matches nothing the generator can find, and without this line the list says Mistral reaches no model that eight of the nine cells of its column name.

mistral-large-3._note: Mistral ships the model as mistral-large-2512; the model card names it Mistral Large 3. Its catalogue does not say so. OpenRouter stood here too, with mistralai/mistral-large-2512, and the EU host this installation is bound to lists no such id: its mistralai/mistral-large and mistralai/mistral-large-2407 are Mistral Large 2 by OpenRouter's own description of both. The line was removed on 2026-09-22 rather than pointed at either, because naming a different model here is the one thing this block exists to prevent. On 2026-10-27 the EU host's catalogue (https://eu.openrouter.ai/api/v1/models) lists mistralai/mistral-large-2512, and OpenRouter describes it there as "Mistral Large 3 2512" with "675B total" parameters, which is the model card's model; the line stands again.
